original_card.question: Can one exact all-size/compiler, precision, hosting or restoration implication be proved or falsified?
methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.
Find an exact counterexample at the claimed interface boundary.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected review scope and choose one exact all-size or precision implication.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write its quantified inputs and conclusion; find a missing hypothesis or construct a minimal exact adversarial instance.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Finite supplier improvements are useful only under the retained transfer obligations.
allowed_variations: Choose one tape, precision, hosting or restoration lemma.
scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.

actual_scope: Is the finer-constant Mercator logarithm engine (fine_mercator.py, blob 29699092) used by open PRs 1479 and 1485 to certify 1e-120 complex endpoint brackets an outward enclosure, and does any defect affect their pinned m=73 inputs?
scope_change_reason: The card asks for an all-size/precision implication. This audits a narrower certified-arithmetic implication (engine output encloses log x) behind open conditional-kappa candidates, because reading the engine exposed an exact parity defect with a concrete counterexample. It is labelled as an arithmetic-certificate audit, not a transfer lemma.
bottleneck_link: Side result for review reliability: candidate kappa refinements rest on certified moment enclosures; an unsound engine copy weakens their two-engine certification and could certify false rejections if reused.
stop_rule: Stop after an exact counterexample, the pinned-input impact check and a verified repair; do not replay the full PR admissions.
evidence: verify.py: exact false lower bounds of fine_mercator.logarithm at 43, 189, 352; all 73 pinned m=73 inputs valid (min margin ~0.029*2^-800); LOGN=801 repair valid; vendored and retained sources pinned.
author: Philippe Van Velzen
ai_assistance: Substantial assistance from Claude (Anthropic, Claude Code) for code reading, verifier and text; results checked by the exact verifier.

open_questions.question: Do PR1479/PR1485's 1e-120 endpoint certificates still pass with the repaired engine (LOGN=801)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The PRs claim certification by two engines; only the sound one currently carries the reject lower bounds in principle.
open_questions.first_step: Rerun each PR's check_moment for native and conservative complex sides with LOGN=801.
open_questions.blocked_by: Requires the PR packages' own replay; best done by the PR authors.

open_questions.question: Should new certified-arithmetic engine copies include a parity/tail self-test against an independent oracle?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A one-line check would have caught this defect before reuse.
open_questions.first_step: Add an assertion that LOGN is odd or compare logarithm(3/2) with an atanh enclosure.
open_questions.blocked_by: Frozen packages must not be retrofitted; applies to new packages only.
